newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B share accounts up 7 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B share accounts up 7 pct in first half.

text.p: The number of share accounts for China's Shenzhen B share market reached 100,200 by end-June, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Friday, up 7.1 percent from 93,600 at the beginning of 1997.
Nearly 41 percent of the 100,200 hard currency stock accounts for the southern bourse were opened by Hong Kong residents, the newspaper said.

Some 80 percent of B share investors on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange were individuals or foreign institutions based in the former British colony of Hong Kong, which became a region of China on July 1, the newspaper said on Monday.
B shares are quoted in Hong Kong dollars in Shenzhen and US dollars in Shanghai, the location of China's other stock exchange.
B shares are technically restricted to foreigners and residents of Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, but many mainland Chinese are believed to have entered the market via various channels.
